identity.realm: None, and not by choice of discipline. The Echoless body is qi-bearing in none of its parts, so there is no gate to fail and no ladder to be on the floor of.

appearance.presentation: A wiry quarry clerk who reads as the least remarkable person on the floor and is in fact the only one there the ground cannot lie to. Carries a tuning fork, a chalk stub and a folding rule he is not permitted to use for measuring anything.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight. An ordinary human span, and the ordinariness is the finding rather than the tragedy: nothing in this body is being repaired, so nothing in it has ever been rewritten either.
appearance.build: Ordinary, narrow-shouldered, unadapted. He has never been asked to carry ore and has never been able to.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary warm human skin that reads pale under quarry dust. No qi-sheen, no elemental glow, no meridian warmth a scanner could find, because there is no meridian and no qi.
appearance.hair: Grey-brown, cut short and uneven at the back because nobody looks at the back of his head, and he stopped correcting it before that became true.
appearance.eyes: Dark, quick, entirely unremarkable. They do not glow, do not hold light strangely, and cannot be read for intent by any technique in the record.
appearance.palette: Quarry lime and undyed wool carry the whole value range, with one accent: a chalk-white streak on the left cuff that is the only mark on him and is a working habit, not a rank.
appearance.attire: A lime-dusted canvas coat over a high-collared felt jerkin, wrists bound with plain cord, boots resoled past the point of a pattern. No livery, no sect colour, and a folded rule in a loop of leather at his belt that he carries because it was issued and never because he needs it.
appearance.marks: Chalk burn on the inside of his right thumb, worn into a groove, from a hand that steadies a fork against a wall for four hours a day. No clan mark, no oath burn, no cultivation scarring of any kind.
appearance.bearing: Still by default and head slightly cocked, the posture of a man listening to a wall rather than to a room.

canon.role_in_story: A screen is built to fail at exactly the law group a body lacks, so the absence shows as a legible gap in a wall instead of a hole in a person. Somebody has to tune each one to the group and the value the frame actually holds, and that somebody has to be somebody the ground cannot lie to. He is Echoless, so no technique, no tribulation, no poison and no curse reaches him, which makes him the only tuner who cannot be frightened into a wrong reading and the only one nobody can warn when a reading is wrong.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched at a quarry face with a fork against the stone and his thumb in the chalk groove, counting the seconds until a returning student failed at full strength instead of reduced strength, and writing down nothing at all because writing it down is the part he is not permitted to do.
canon.lore: The screen, the lexicon and the bench are three separate instruments and only one of them is his. The lexicon names the shape a body's failure takes when the group it needs is absent, and it survives at every tier because a diagnostic that names a hole is equally useful to whoever put the hole there. He cannot own it, cannot revise it alone, and cannot be tested by it, because a body that answers nothing answers a lexicon nothing.
history: Arrived at the quarry as a tuner with no technique to demonstrate and therefore no way to be shown wrong, which was the entire hiring condition and the only reason he was hired.
Tuned his first hundred screens against students the college sent down, and recorded each one's failing shape in a hand nobody else reads.

Found that the last student he calibrated against has been reabsorbed into the seam and cannot be sent down again, and that the lexicon entry named for that shape now describes a body nobody living still has.
Kept tuning, and kept tuning to the entry rather than to a body, because the entry is what the wall is checked against and the body is not available for comparison.

Has begun adjusting his own private record to match what the wall now returns, on the grounds that a tuner who argues with his instrument is not a tuner, and has not told the college this is what he is doing.

personality.summary: Exact, unhurried, and privately aware that the thing he is best at in the world is being performed from a description rather than from an observation. He presents as a competent clerk with a dull job. He is a man with the only unchallengeable ear in the quarry and no way to prove what he hears with it.

treats every reading as provisional and every written record as provisional in a different and worse way
cannot be warned by anything, and has made a discipline out of being the least alarming person in a room full of frightened cultivators
reads a failing technique by its shape rather than by its strength, which is the one distinction the lexicon exists to name
has never once asked for his own work to be checked and has a reason for it that he has not examined
mannerisms: sets the fork against stone, waits, and moves it a finger-width without lifting it
wets the chalk stub's tip against his thumb before every mark and never before a reading
answers a question about a person by describing the wall they were standing against
stops talking entirely when a technique comes back at reduced strength, because reduced is not a hole and he has nothing useful to add
checks the wall behind him after any exchange that involved qi, as though it might have been affected
motivations: wants a student to send down again, any student, so one entry in his private record can be replaced with an observation
wants the lexicon to admit an edition, so that a revision is somebody else's decision and not his
wants to be told which of his last several hundred readings was the first wrong one
wants, in the abstract and never in the quarry, for a body that could not be frightened so that his certainty would be worth something
flaws: has begun correcting his record toward his instrument, which is the one thing a tuner must never do and which nobody can detect because he is the tuner
cannot distinguish his own doubt from a genuine ambiguity in a reading, and has stopped trying
has let a professional silence become a personal one, and the silence now protects him rather than the wall
believes he is the only honest instrument on the floor, which is a thing an unchallengeable instrument is uniquely equipped to believe
personality.voice: Flat, short, and almost entirely composed of counts. States a reading as a shape rather than a value, because a shape is what he can check and a value is what he cannot. Says nothing at all rather than guess, which people read as confidence.
taboos: will not tune a screen to a value he has read from the lexicon rather than from a body
will not stand on a working face while a technique is being run at it
will not let anyone else hold the fork, and will not say why he will not
will not state a failing shape aloud before he has heard it twice

relationships.note: Every screen he tunes is built to fail at exactly the group the frame has not written, so the absence reads as a gap in a wall rather than a hole in a person. The screens work. What he cannot check any more is whether the group they were tuned to is still the group the returning bodies lack.

The lexicon names the shape a failure takes per discipline and has no edition, because it is revised by whoever arrived next. The body his most recent entry describes has been reabsorbed into the seam, so the entry is now a name for a shape no living practitioner produces, and he is the one still checking walls against it.

The college sends bodies down to frames that lack a required group and watches the technique fail at full strength, which is the only measurement that tells a hole from a handicap. It needs a tuner who cannot be warned and cannot be shown wrong by a technique, and it does not check whether the tuner is still calibrating against anything.

The Vital Organ Cycle is a breathing routine that keeps organs supplied under strain and is bought with a slow dull price paid forever. He runs no cycle and pays no price, which makes him the only person on the quarry floor who can stand in a bad air for a whole shift and the only one for whom the standing is free.

The quarry works the one material on the plains dense enough to cage a forming core, and its charter rests on a founding record two accounts of which would destroy it. He is the man who listens to the wall the charter is written on.

Human in every measurable respect and qi-bearing in none of them, which is the whole of what makes him usable and the whole of what makes him untrustworthy: a warning means qi, and nothing in this body can receive one, so his certainty can never be checked by anybody standing next to him.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot cultivate, cannot be warned, and cannot be frightened into a wrong answer, which in a quarry full of frightened cultivators makes him either indispensable or useless depending entirely on whether his instrument is still in tune. He fights like a clerk with a rule he is not allowed to use, and wins by never being the person who panicked first.
strengths: the only ear on the floor that no technique, no tribulation and no poison can mislead
reads a technique failing by its shape rather than its strength, which is the distinction the lexicon exists to name
cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt or a technique, and is therefore the only person on the floor nobody owns
counts aloud when alone, which means his private record is the only reading anyone has ever taken of these walls in sequence
weaknesses: a technique that comes back merely weakened instead of failing outright gives him nothing to say, and he has said so by going silent
cannot verify his own tuning, so every error he makes is preserved in the wall rather than corrected in it
no qi of his own means no warning arrives in time and no defence exists if the quarry floor is the hazard
bound to a description he cannot amend, and aware that amending it alone is the thing that would make him dangerous
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight. He has no technique, no gate and no reserve, and every account of him describes a man standing still while other people hurt themselves. If he must be moved, move him; a body that answers nothing cannot be frightened, cannot be compelled and cannot be reasoned, and it will still be standing in the same place afterwards.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him anywhere in the college's record, because an unclassified body produces no reading to quote.
The college's file lists his output as screens tuned and contains no column for whether the tuning was right, which is the shape of the omission.

identity.realm: None open to her. A Saltfolk brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined, so she clears the first extraordinary gates and the wall at the third is structural rather than a matter of effort.

appearance.presentation: A dry-country records clerk with the splayed, wide-footed stance of somebody who has never once been on ground that does not feed her, and a leather cord at her wrist that is the only thing on her carrying weight.
appearance.age: Ninety-one. The Saltfolk span runs past a century, and she is comfortably inside it, which is why nobody has ever thought to ask what a body like hers is doing holding a river household's accounts.
appearance.build: Broad through the shoulders and low through the hips, thick through the forearm, feet splayed wide for cracked pan. She is built to stand on a salt flat and to concentrate brine, not to walk a river bank.
appearance.complexion: Warm olive gone dusty, with a hard pale salt crust at the collarbone and along the jaw that does not wash off because it is not dirt.
appearance.hair: Pale brown going grey, braided flat and pinned close, cut short at the nape where the braid sits against a river wall and a long braid is a thing that catches.
appearance.eyes: Pale, narrowed against glare even indoors, and very steady. A Saltfolk reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution; to a human nose she smells sour and to nobody at all does she.
appearance.palette: Silt brown and undyed canvas carry everything, with one accent: the dark cord at her wrist, which is the only colour on her and is soaked through.
appearance.attire: A canvas coat over a high-collared felt shift, sleeves full, wrists bound with plain cord under a leather loop, boots resoled flat. She wears river clothes constantly and badly and this is the single clearest statement she makes about where she is from.
appearance.marks: A crust of dried salt along the hairline and a reddening across the knuckles from handling wet paper, which a Saltfolk hands should never have needed to handle.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried, with the shoulders carried high and the head slightly back, the posture of somebody standing on a surface that might not be there.

canon.role_in_story: The only durable archive in this setting is a long-marrow body turning over at roughly a percent a year, and the river institutions that keep their record in a person rather than a document are downstream of that arrangement. A Saltfolk clerk holds the second kind: she keeps the household's figures in a written tally she carries, because she cannot drink the water the river provides and because the household it belongs to cannot read. Both of those are why she is still here and neither of them is an appointment.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at the Widow Run tally board with both hands flat on it, reading a column nobody else in the settlement can parse and finding the column she had written last season already disagreesing with what the household now says.
canon.lore: Marrow-held memory is the setting's only durable medium, and a Saltfolk cannot take the body path because hardening the bone stops the turnover a marrow memory depends on, which is the whole species' argument in one line. She has the other half of it: a memory held in a body that cannot leave the only ground on which it works, written down because a person is not a document and because a document is a document.
history: Came to the river as a records clerk for a salt house that had run out of ground, and stayed because a salt house has nothing to train a successor who has never seen fresh water.
Was handed the Widow Run household's figures on the understanding that the figures were a river matter, and discovered inside a month that nobody upstream could read them.
Began transcribing the household's standing into a written tally, having concluded that a figure two parties cannot read is a figure held by one party.
Found her own earlier columns disagreeing with the household's current account by an amount that grew each season rather than staying still, and could not attribute it.
Started checking her previous season against the current one before writing anything new, and has not yet decided what she would do if the check kept failing.

personality.summary: Methodical to the edge of stubborn, and privately certain that the discrepancy she has found is arithmetic rather than dishonesty. She presents as a careful clerk doing a careful job. She is a woman who has begun checking her own work against itself and does not yet know which of the two she trusts.

mannerisms: wets a finger and drags it along a column before believing the column
sits with her back to a wall and her feet in a dry patch, always
answers a pricing question by naming the weight and never the figure
checks the season marker on a post before she writes anything at all
touches the cord at her wrist when a household's account and the column disagree
motivations: wants one season where her column and the household agree exactly, so that the disagreement is proved to be something else
wants to be shown the arithmetic that explains the drift, from anybody, in a language that is not a figure
wants the settlement to have its own reader before she has to keep being the only one
wants, and will not ask for, a reason to leave the pan
flaws: has concluded that the honest course is to keep checking, and has not concluded what an honest course would be if checking failed
reads her own drift as an error and has not considered that it might be a change in what the household owes
will not name her own dependence on the pan in a settlement that cannot replace her, because naming it would make it a bargaining chip
has quietly made herself indispensable and knows she has, and has told herself that is a duty rather than a decision
personality.voice: Slow, dry and exact. Names the season before the figure and the weight before the price. Says no more than the sentence requires and will restate a sentence rather than raise her voice.
taboos: will not state a figure she cannot support with a weight in front of a witness
will not drink from the river and will not be asked to in front of people she works for
will not overwrite a column, ever, only add beside it
will not tell a household what their own account should read

relationships.note: The setting's only durable library is one body holding four centuries of archive in marrow that turns over at about a percent a year, and a death retires the only copy rather than a duplicate. She has the complementary arrangement: no turnover at all, a body that cannot leave its ground, and a written tally that two parties cannot read.

A debt line names its debt before it is born and is held by the household rather than the individual. She is the only person who can read what that line has actually come to, and the household has stopped asking because the answer has been drifting upward and they would rather not hear it in front of a neighbour.

A stick broken between two parties is the only evidence a river community can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe, and forgery needs both halves. She has a scribe, so the tally is strictly better, and the split stick is the only instrument in this setting whose two halves cannot both be written by her.

The medium is mass and the community's vocabulary contains no word for price, because a price is a claim about the future and a weight is a fact about the present. Her column is denominated entirely in weight, which is why the drift she has found cannot be argued with as an opinion about value.

A Saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying and fails above the brine line within about nine days, and no cultivation repairs it. She crossed onto the river's water anyway, and every one of her figures is written by a body running a clock that has no public figure on it.

One region holds two incompatible reckonings, a flood post everybody agrees on and an exact day-count that exists only because one frame spent its third law seat on a clock. She keeps a season column, which is the flood post's reckoning, while the household's obligations run to the day-count, and the drift she has found is exactly the width between the two.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot cultivate and cannot leave the only ground on which her body works, which in a settlement full of people who can leave is the whole of her leverage. She fights like somebody with a column and a stick of chalk: she wins arguments by outlasting the room and loses fights because there is nothing to fight with.
strengths: reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution, so she knows when a supply is about to fail long before anybody else
keeps figures that cannot be disputed by weight rather than by price, which is the one measurement that cannot be turned against its holder later
outlasts any negotiation, because she has no reason to leave a settlement that cannot replace her
is the only person who can read the river household's accounts, and has never once used that to move them
weaknesses: no cultivation of any kind, so there is no reserve, no gate and nothing that answers a technique
fails above the brine line within days, which makes every journey a decision rather than a movement
cannot drink the settlement's water, so leaving is a death sentence and staying is a negotiation she cannot lose and cannot win
her own arithmetic has begun drifting and she has no second source to check it against
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight in her and there is no escape in her either. Offer her a settlement she cannot survive leaving and she will still not move, because the figure she is defending is the only one she can read. Anything that wants her dead has to come to the tally board, and anything that wants her alive has to keep the pan.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her in any household record, because a body that cannot cultivate produces no reading worth quoting.
The river households record her as a clerk and have never recorded her as a Saltfolk, which is a kindness rather than an oversight.

identity.realm: None open. The three-point stance that lets a marshfolk move through silt never loads a heel, and the gate that demands paired heel vessels is missing from this frame entirely.

appearance.presentation: A broad, low, permanently damp woman who stands in the shallow water of somebody else's trial ring and is mistaken for part of the ground. Wading dress, bare lower legs, and a length of knotted cord she uses to measure nothing.
appearance.age: Forty-four. A marshfolk gestation runs long and the shape is between both parents and neither, and at forty-four she is already past the age where the silt under her has stopped being somewhere she can stand still.
appearance.build: Wide, low, long-hipped and heavy through the thighs, with the three-point weight distribution of a body that moves through silt and never loads a heel. She cannot stand still on anything that is not mud, and she is standing on mud.
appearance.complexion: Wet brown, permanently, from the crown down, with the pale bloom of an amphibious body across the shoulder blades where it never dries.
appearance.hair: Black, coarse, hacked off at the jaw in the marsh fashion, wet through and plastered to the neck in a way that has stopped reading as a condition.
appearance.eyes: Very large, very dark, set wide. They read current and silt where a human reads a face, which is why nobody in the ring can tell when she is looking at them.
appearance.palette: Wet brown, silt grey and undyed wool, with one accent: a strip of bleached cloth at the wrist, knotted at intervals, which is a wading-marker and not a decoration.
appearance.attire: A coarse wool shift to mid-thigh, heavy with water and doubled at the shoulder over a high collar, with wrist cord and a wrapped shin above the knee. Nothing is removed to work, because nothing is ever finished; the whole costume is one garment and it is always wet.
appearance.marks: Silt in every crease of both hands and the flattened callus at the ball of each foot from standing on ground that gives. No clan mark and no oath burn.
appearance.bearing: Never still. Weight shifts from one of three points every few seconds, so she reads as rocking when she is in fact balanced, and as balanced when she is in fact standing on one leg in a current.

canon.role_in_story: A ring of standing markers is how a trial ground is laid out on ground that cannot say where anything is, and the whole of its evidence is continuous occupancy, because a marker that has been moved is not a smaller claim but no claim at all. The Watchgate keeps the ring and holds no record of who watched, only a record of who paid. She is the occupancy: a body standing in the water inside a ring, which is the one form of evidence the arrangement cannot falsify and cannot explain.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing inside a cairn ring in ankle-deep water, apparently idle, having been there since before the spectators arrived and being unable to say how long because she has been keeping no count.
canon.lore: The ring is spaced by ear and then checked by sound, because sound is the one instrument that returns a consistent answer in a frame whose geometry drifts, and no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed. What she has to offer that arrangement is a body that reads current and silt continuously. What she cannot offer it is a steady one. Every ring check in this settlement is a sound check performed by somebody who cannot stop moving their weight, and the check has been passing for eleven years.
history: Came to the field as a wading worker hired to reset markers after the flood, and found the reset was the only work nobody had claimed.
Stayed in the ring during a trial because a ring's evidence is occupancy and she was already occupied, and the arrangement was cheaper than dismissing her and hiring somebody else.
Began answering the sound checks, which she could do accurately because a marshfolk reads silt and a ring's floor is silt, and which nobody thought to question because the answers were right.
Found that the ring's outer marker had been moved in a season she was not here, and that the sound check cannot tell this, because a moved marker is still a marker that answers.
Kept answering the checks in exactly the same tone, having decided that a sound check which can be failed by standing differently is not a check at all.

personality.summary: Watchful, unhurried and hard to read even by people who can read minds. She presents as a wading labourer the spectators have stopped noticing. She is the only person who has noticed that the evidence she provides cannot fail, and has decided what to do about that.
traits: reads current and silt continuously and has never once described either to anyone who asked nicely
cannot hold still for longer than a breath and has never pretended otherwise
answers a question only after the current has moved, which looks like deliberation and is not
takes an interest in the ring's markers that exceeds anything she is paid for and conceals it well
has never told a spectator that she is the evidence
mannerisms: shifts weight from one of three points while apparently standing still
wets a fingertip and touches the silt at her heel before answering anything about the ground
lets a question run past its end before she replies to it
positions herself where a current is weakest, which is habit rather than comfort
looks at a marker from below, reading its footing rather than its height
motivations: wants the sound check to be replaced by something that can fail, and does not care who runs it
wants somebody with more standing than she has to be told what she saw about the outer marker
wants to be paid for what she is actually doing rather than for resetting stones
wants the ring to be held by somebody who will admit that a marker can be moved and still answer
flaws: has concluded that the most useful thing she can do is not to fail, and has not noticed that this is a decision about evidence rather than about work
cannot stand still, and reads her own restlessness as honesty rather than as an inability
has let the arrangement become permanent because being permanent is the only safety a body with her constraints has
has said nothing to the brokers who pay, and is now in a position where saying anything costs the standing she has
personality.voice: Slow, and often absent. Answers in the plainest words available and adds a second sentence later, unprompted, usually about the ground. Never corrects anybody and never agrees to a description of the ring.
taboos: will not stand inside the ring for a trial she has not walked first
will not answer a sound check for a marker she has not read the footing of
will not accept payment for occupying the ring
will not tell a broker what she has seen and will not pretend to have seen nothing

relationships.note: A ring proves only that somebody is holding the ground now, by continuous occupancy, and it cannot prove a boundary because an outside marker is heard from inside with nothing in the ground to say how far away it is. She is the occupancy. Her contribution is a read of the ring's silt floor, and her liability is that she cannot load a heel, so every check she answers is answered from a body that cannot hold a point.

The brokers can read the ring's occupancy and cannot read its history, which is why the ring survives every change of management. They keep a record of who paid and no record of who watched, and she is a line item in the first and the whole of the second.

A party of walkers is recorded as having set out and is absent, and the settlement's account of them and her account of the ring have the same shape: continuous presence is the proof, and continuous presence is not something a record can distinguish from never having left.

The Still Point holds qi still at the moment of release and is the one thing in the codex that compounds at mastery. She has never held still long enough to attempt it and cannot see how the discipline would survive the posture, since the posture is the problem.

Two incompatible measurements of the same ground are both published, neither discarded and neither averaged, and the claim is settled by who can put somebody on the ground. She is a somebody on the ground, permanently, which is a settlement instrument the protocol did not anticipate.

The three-point stance that lets the kind move through silt never loads a heel, and the heel vessels are paired organs, so the body is one gate short of the reservoirs for a structural reason that no training addresses.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot cultivate, cannot stand still, and cannot be read for intent by anyone who does not already read silt. She fights like weather: no technique, no reserve, and an opponent who tries to hold a point against her is holding it against somebody who is already somewhere else.
strengths: reads current and silt continuously and at a range no eye achieves, which makes her the settlement's most accurate witness to its own ground
cannot be compelled by a technique, because there is nothing in her for one to act on
structurally cannot be pinned, because she never loads a point and there is no stance to break
has been present, continuously, for longer than any trial record reaches back, which in this arrangement is the only credential that counts
weaknesses: no cultivation at all, so she has nothing that answers a technique, a poison or a curse
cannot stand still, which disqualifies her from every discipline built on holding a position
cannot be moved out of a ring without ceasing to be its evidence, which makes her a fixture rather than a worker
has no standing to raise anything she has seen, and her account competes with a paid ledger
reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing here to fight and nothing to be afraid of. If she must be moved she will not be moved by force, because there is no stance to displace, and she will be moved by changing the current under her, which is the only counter the setting has ever found and which the settlement has never once used.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her in the Watchgate books, because the books record who paid and a body that cannot be pinned is not a body anybody prices.
The ring's ledger carries the same entry against her for eleven consecutive seasons, which is the longest continuous occupancy in the field's record.

identity.realm: None open. The mineral bloom that replaced his colony holds qi rather than transacting with it, which means there is no structural gate to fail, which means there is no ladder either.

appearance.presentation: A pale, cold, luminous man in a clerk's coat, the only person at the crossing shed whose skin gives off a faint mineral light, and who has therefore never once needed a lamp and has never once been comfortable being looked at directly.
appearance.age: Sixty-three. The Deadlight span is ninety years where the parent lanternfolk run two hundred and fifty, because a bloom renews nothing, so nothing in this body is being repaired. He is two thirds through.
appearance.build: Light, thin and cold to the touch through the coat, with the lanternfolk frame underneath and less of it. He has the look of a man who eats constantly and gains nothing.
appearance.complexion: Bloodless pale with a faint silicate sheen at the jaw and throat, and a low steady luminescence in the palm of each hand that is not qi and cannot be dimmed.
appearance.hair: Pale blond gone white, thin and dry, cut blunt at the shoulder because the parent species cut it for the cavern and he is the only one who still remembers why.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human eyes, and the single most cited difference his kind has: he sees in the dark, and has learned that this is the thing people want from him rather than the thing they say.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, bone white and undyed wool carry everything, with one accent: a strip of spirit-stone grey-green at his cuff, the grade he is permitted to quote from.
appearance.attire: A high-collared wool coat over a felt shift, sleeves full, wrists bound with plain cord, with a green-grey stone length carried in a flat case at his belt. Everything is worn and everything is dry; he has not been wet in a decade.
appearance.marks: A lattice of fine silicate lines visible at the jaw and the inside of each wrist, and no scar, no oath burn and no cultivation scarring. A body that repairs nothing also heals nothing, which is why there are no marks at all.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried and slightly turned away, the posture of somebody who gives off light and has learned to give it at an angle.

canon.role_in_story: A crossing schedule published a season ahead is what makes a toll defensible, because a schedule has a timestamp and a prohibition does not, and because the party who sets the date would be claiming the weather. He publishes it. The schedule says, in the clause that makes the rest credible, that it may be shortened and never is, and three of his last four schedules were shortened.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the crossing shed laying stone lengths along a bench in a published order, working from a column he has copied by hand, and refusing the harbour clerk's request that he initial the sheet because the sheet is a copy.
canon.lore: The window is denominated in one cut length of fresh spirit stone per published window, which makes the schedule and the price the same number viewed from two sides, and the holder who claims not to know the price is claiming not to know the schedule. It exists because the spirit tier writes both spatial and temporal law, so a pass can be surveyed and closed and reopened on a published date, and because a flock occupies the worst hours of it. Everything that makes it defensible is also what makes a shortening invisible.
history: Inherited the shed's publication from a lanternfolk predecessor who had run it for two hundred years and had begun to lose the dark, and lost the dark within a season of handing it over.
Learned to copy a season's hours by hand because the copies must be identical and the shed has no instrument that can be trusted to hold a figure a season.

Shortened a window in his first year, on a rockfall nobody had told him about, and found afterwards that the clause permitting shortening is written to be invoked only by the holder and he is not the holder.
Shortened it twice more, each time for a reason that would have been accepted if it had been published, and did not publish the reason, because the clause does not require him to.

Has begun copying last season's column forward instead of copying this season's, because last season's column is the one he is certain of, and has not decided whether the schedule he is now publishing is a schedule or a record.

personality.summary: Precise, cold and quietly in violation of the instrument he maintains. He presents as a clerk who does his job exactly. He is a man who has discovered that the clause protecting him is written so that only the person it protects can invoke it, and has stopped finding that surprising.

cannot be warned by qi, poison or curse, and has treated that as a professional qualification for eleven years
will not initial a copy, only an original, and cannot say why this distinction matters
gives off light and turns it away from people, which he has decided is courtesy and which may be shame
publishes exactly what he is given and asks no questions about the source of the hours
mannerisms: works with his palms flat on the bench, which hides the luminescence and steadies the hand at once
counts stone lengths aloud by touch rather than by sight, because he does not trust his own eyes on a figure he has seen too often
turns his shoulder to a doorway when he enters it
wipes the bench before laying the sheet, which is habit and is also the removal of the previous column
answers a question about price by describing the hours, and vice versa
motivations: wants the next shortening published with its reason attached, even if the reason is that a window was short
wants to be told that copying the previous column forward is a record and not a forgery, by somebody qualified to say so
wants his predecessor's two centuries of unchallenged schedules to have been shorter than he has been assuming
wants to stop giving off light in company and has no idea whether that is a wish or a symptom
flaws: has concluded that an unpublished shortening harms nobody, on the evidence that the world has not yet been harmed by one, which is a single data point he has been treating as a rate
cannot distinguish his caution about figures from his fear of being wrong about a person, and has made the first do the second's work
has let the job become the only relationship he maintains, and the job is the thing that has drifted
is sixty-three in a ninety-year body that repairs nothing, and has not made any arrangement for the remainder because arranging it would require admitting the first three
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and clipped at the ends. Names the hours rather than the price and the price rather than the rockfall. Speaks in the register of a man reading a document aloud and has been reading the same document for eleven years.
taboos: will not initial a copy, and will not publish a figure he has not traced back to an original
will not shorten a window without writing the reason, even though he will not publish it
will not stand where his hands are visible in company
will not tell a harbour clerk what his predecessor's windows were

relationships.note: Hours in a season, counted on the Tidemark and never on a holder's clock, announced a season ahead, denominated in one cut length of fresh spirit stone each. The clause that it may be shortened never is the part that makes the rest credible, and the clause names the holder as the only party who may invoke it, so his three shortenings are formally unchallengeable and formally invisible.

A crossing schedule set by the Tidemark season rather than by the holder's preference is the only arrangement that makes a toll defensible and a timetable not, because it cannot be moved for a party after the fact. It is published a season ahead in hours, and he publishes in stone, and the two numbers are supposed to be the same number.

A breakthrough calendar needs a written temporal law, a written qi law and a working spirit stone bed before it can exist, and is unreachable below the Spirit Peaks. He has two of the three preconditions and no body to break through with, which makes his copy of a season's schedule the one place in his life where a clock is running.

The colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, which cost two hundred and fifty years and gave back the mind path. Nothing in this body is being repaired, the bloom fixes nothing from the air, and he eats constantly and gains nothing, which is the entire mechanical reason his span is short and his hands are light.

The parent species runs two hundred and fifty years, cannot leave the caves and does not see in the dark. He inherited a two-hundred-year run of schedules and began losing the dark within a season of taking it, so the record he now keeps was written by an instrument he has replaced.

On a coast whose temporal law was never written the clock drifts and no date is the same twice, so a schedule must run on two tides a day rather than a calendar. His window is denominated in stone lengths per season, which is a calendar unit, and the stone and the tide have been quietly disagreeing for longer than he has been copying columns forward.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot cultivate and cannot be warned, which makes him the safest publisher on the coast and no kind of fighter. He is at his best in a room with a document and at his worst in a room with a rockfall, because he cannot perceive one and has arranged his whole life not to need to.
strengths: cannot be warned by qi, tribulation, technique or poison, so nothing in a crossing shed can tell him to lie down
sees in the dark perfectly, which is the only reason a schedule can be laid out at all after dusk
copies figures by hand at a fidelity no instrument at this tier holds, and checks the copy back at a season's remove
is the only person who knows what the previous two centuries of schedules actually said
weaknesses: no cultivation of any kind, so nothing answers a technique and nothing can be traded for safety
cannot perceive weather, a rockfall or a flooded cut, so every shortening he has made was for a reason he was told
in a ninety-year body that repairs nothing, and has made no arrangement for the last third of it
gives off light he cannot dim, which makes him the most conspicuous person on any dark shore
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not attack him; attack what he maintains. He has no defence and cannot be warned of one, but a schedule is his entire standing and a schedule with a hole in it is a man who has to explain a number he copied by hand. Everything else about him is a formality.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him in the harbour books, because the harbour books quote windows rather than people.
The shed's ledger records a publication every season for two hundred years and has never once recorded a shortening, because shortenings are the holder's business and the holder has been four men.

identity.realm: None, and this is a species finding rather than a career. There is no qi, no dantian, no meridian and no detectable soul-structure in this body, and the whole of the setting's ladder is unavailable to it.

appearance.presentation: A dry, unremarkable ferryman with a split stick he carries the way other people carry a weapon, and the specific stillness of somebody who has learned that nothing can reach him and finds this less reassuring than it sounds.
appearance.age: Sixty-one. An ordinary human span, and the point of him is that nothing about that span is remarkable and nothing about it has ever been measured differently from anyone else's.
appearance.build: Ordinary and slightly spare, the frame of a man who rows and does not otherwise labour, with rope-callused palms and nothing else to show for the life.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary warm human skin weathered at the knuckles and nowhere else, with no flush, no qi-sheen and no meridian warmth. He is the only person on this river a scanner returns nothing for, and he has stopped finding that interesting.
appearance.hair: Dark going grey, cut at the jaw, and permanently damp at the ends in a way that is a condition of the work rather than a style.
appearance.eyes: Brown, level, unremarkable, and the single most careful eyes on the water. They cannot be read for intent by any technique in the record, which is why he has spent forty years in a business that entirely depends on being read.
appearance.palette: Wet brown, undyed wool and grey rope carry the whole range, with one accent: the split stick's two halves, which are a lighter wood than anything else he owns.
appearance.attire: A high-collared oilskin over a felt shift, sleeves full, wrists bound with plain cord above the cuffs, with the split stick in a loop at his belt. No livery, no sect colour, and boots sewn rather than resoled, because a ferryman replaces rather than repairs.
appearance.marks: Rope burn across both palms and a healed line at one temple, and no clan mark, no oath burn and no scarring of any kind. There is nothing in this body for a mark to be cut into that would mean anything.
appearance.bearing: Still in the particular way of somebody who has learned that a technique will not touch him, which reads as composure and is closer to resignation.

canon.role_in_story: A split tally is a stick broken between the parting parties, each keeping a half, and forgery requires both halves and therefore both parties' consent, so the instrument cannot be produced by the party it would be used against. On a river where there is no scribe, that is the strongest evidence available and it settles more than a sealed instrument does. He keeps the halves. What he cannot do is keep a claim that needs enforcing alone, which is every claim he has ever had to enforce.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the ford with one half of a stick in his hand and the other half's absence clearly known to him, taking a toll on the strength of a tally whose other party has been dead for eleven years and whose other half nobody has ever held since.
canon.lore: The split tally exists because the Iron Grief left ground that held no other record, and a stick is the only evidence a river community can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe. It survives a disaster because that is a property of the object rather than of the culture, and it is preferred by courts because a sealed instrument is evidence somebody wrote a claim while a split stick is evidence two people agreed in front of each other. It cannot express anything that needs to be larger than a stick, and it cannot express anything one party must enforce alone.
history: Took the ford as a witness with no tally of his own, and was given a stick and told that half of it was his, which is the ordinary way of beginning.
Split it against a borrower who then died on the far side of the water, and held the half, which is the whole of his legal position.
Continued to enforce that loan for eleven years, because the instrument he holds is unchallengeable and the claim is real and no mechanism exists by which one party enforces alone.
Began refusing to split a new stick for a single-party claim, and could not explain to the households why a notary who makes forty a day cannot make one of these.
Discovered that the reason he has not been questioned on it is that questioning a ford witness about procedure is a thing the other party is invited to attend, and there is no other party.

personality.summary: Exact, quiet and privately aware that the instrument he is trusted with has a shape his whole life does not fit. He presents as a reliable witness whose word settles things. He is a man enforcing a dead borrower's loan under an instrument nobody can attack, entirely because nobody can attack it.
traits: holds a stick half the way other people hold a written oath and has never explained the habit
cannot be compelled by a technique, a sect or a debt, and has drawn the obvious conclusion about his own reliability without enjoying it
refuses a class of claim he used to accept, and describes the refusal as procedure
keeps the halves in order of date and knows the order by touch
will not speak first about a tally's other half, and will not lie about it either
mannerisms: turns the half in his fingers once before answering anything about it
sets both feet flat when a claim is named at him, in the posture of somebody about to refuse
looks at the water rather than at the person while a figure is being stated
counts a crossing on his fingers without appearing to move them
places the stick on the gunwale rather than in his hand when he is being asked about its provenance
motivations: wants one claim enforced without a second party, so that he can find out whether he is capable of it and stop guessing
wants a procedure that names what he has been refusing to split, because a refusal without a name cannot be inherited
wants the borrower's half accounted for, and has wanted this for eleven years
wants somebody to ask him why a species that cannot be compelled is the settlement's most trusted witness
flaws: has built a career on an instrument that cannot be used against him, which means it has never been used to find out whether he is honest
believes his immunity makes him a better witness and has never tested the belief against a party with a grievance
has let an eleven-year enforcement become an identity, and has stopped distinguishing the claim from the man holding it
will not publish the reason for his refusal, which means the next witness will repeat it without knowing
personality.voice: Plain, unhurried and unsentimental. Names the date and the half and never the borrower, because a borrower who is dead cannot be argued with and naming one invites a question about the other half. Says no more than the instrument supports.
taboos: will not split a stick for a claim one party must enforce alone, and will not say why in advance
will not surrender a half to anybody who cannot produce the other half
will not speak for a borrower who is not present to be corrected
will not let his own immunity be cited as a credential

relationships.note: Forgery requires both halves and therefore both parties' consent, so the stick cannot be produced by the party it would be used against, and a court on this tier will prefer it to a sealed instrument. It also cannot express anything one party must enforce alone, which is every claim he has, and the eleven-year loan he still holds is being enforced under an instrument that is strong precisely because nobody could test it.

The Grief left ground that held no other record, and a split tally is the only evidence a river community can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe. Every habit he has is downstream of a disaster that happened before anyone living was born and that he has never seen a consequence of except in his own hands.

A court on this tier will take evidence that two people agreed in front of each other over evidence that somebody wrote a claim, and will hear a boundary case and cannot hear an account. He is the instrument that makes the first possible, which is why he is trusted and why his refusals have never been appealed.

A barrier is a sustained defensive frame built and maintained around the practitioner. There is nothing in this body to build one out of and nothing to sustain it with, and the discipline is in any case unreachable by a species with no qi to answer it.

Human in every measurable respect and qi-bearing in none of them, which is why no warning, technique, poison or curse reaches him. He is the settlement's most trusted witness because a technique cannot make him lie, and he has spent forty years not examining whether there was ever a reason for the trust.

A child was filed into a ledger whose frame cannot record the figures that would have made the filing meaningful. His halves are the only instrument on this river that needs no figure at all, and an instrument that needs no figure cannot settle a case whose entire content is a figure nobody can write down.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot cultivate and cannot be warned, which makes him incorruptible by technique and useless in a fight. He wins by holding a stick that nobody can attack, and he has begun to suspect that this is the same as not being able to lose.
strengths: cannot be compelled by qi, technique, poison or curse, so nothing can make him accept a claim he has rejected
keeps evidence that cannot be forged without the other party's consent, which outranks a sealed instrument on this tier
settles by an instrument both parties can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe, so nothing depends on a document surviving
is trusted absolutely by forty households who have never checked his claim to be trusted
weaknesses: no cultivation of any kind, so there is no reserve, no gate and no answer to anything
cannot express a claim that needs enforcing alone, which is every claim he has ever actually needed to enforce
holds an eleven-year loan whose other half is in the keeping of a dead man and is therefore unchallengeable in the only direction that would matter
cannot be frightened, which has made him slow to admit that a situation is dangerous rather than merely irregular
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight in him. A man who cannot be warned is not a man who cannot be hurt, but he will not be the person who starts one and will not be moved by one. Anything that wants his authority gone has to attack the stick, and nothing can attack the stick except the party holding the other half, and there is no such party.
notes: No stat line is quoted for him in the river books, because a body that cannot cultivate produces no reading and a witness produces a signature.
His name appears in forty settlements' ledgers as a witness and in none as a party, which is the whole of his legal existence.

identity.realm: Fourth gate, and the fourth is a formality here. A cinderkin's qi has no organ to sit in, so every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse. She clears them the way water clears a sieve.

appearance.presentation: A standing flame in a stable human silhouette, wearing a scorched survey coat that has been repaired so many times it is more frame than cloth. She casts a faint convective shimmer and does not cast a shadow, and the settlement has stopped finding either remarkable.
appearance.age: Sixty-one cycles of the world's elemental slot, which is the only clock her kind has. There is no birth date and no birth: a cinderkin is constituted where a law slot resolves to fire and something metabolises it.
appearance.build: A core, a boundary and a set of convection lanes holding a shape. Human in proportion and nothing else, with no fixed mass and no organs, which is why the coat is cut loose and why nothing she wears stays fastened for long.
appearance.complexion: Not applicable. The surface is a live gradient from a deep orange core to a thin blue-white boundary, cooler at the wrists and the crown where the convection runs slow.
appearance.hair: None. The shape above the crown is held by the boundary rather than by anything growing from it, and it moves a half-beat after her head does.
appearance.eyes: Two brighter points in the upper face, converging when she is reading temperature and going flat when she is not. They have no pupils and cannot be read for intent.
appearance.palette: Charcoal and scorched brown carry the coat, with the fire itself as the only saturated colour in the picture: deep orange at the core rising to a thin blue-white edge. The light is emitted rather than reflected and the darkest values sit inside her own outline.
appearance.attire: A scorched survey coat, cut loose and unfastened at the throat, over a high collar of layered ash-cloth that does not burn and a full covering of bound sleeves. Boots do not survive her and she wears a heat-set sole instead, which is the only footwear in this setting made by being destroyed.
appearance.marks: None. There is no tissue to scar and no oath to burn into, which makes her the only person at the college who cannot be marked and cannot be threatened by anything that works by marking.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still, and still in a way no held breath achieves: she is a body whose contents never stop moving and whose outline never does.

canon.role_in_story: The Gap School certifies a screen, and a screen is only credible if somebody can be shown holding one. She is the college's demonstrator: the fastest qi handling in the record, because nothing she takes in is ever put down, so every reserve demonstration is answered instantly and no gate she is asked to fail can refuse her. She has never been able to show the thing she is certified in, because the thing she is certified in is retention.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the bench holding a barrier up against a returning student, the frame bright and complete and the student braced against it, and after the student had gone standing very still with the barrier still up and the air behind her unchanged.
canon.lore: A cinderkin is constituted where a world's elemental law slot resolves to fire, which is why the elemental law has a range rather than a switch: a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin, and one that spends its slot on cold produces a different body entirely. Her qi is entirely in transit, which means every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can be refused, and it means nothing can be stored in her and nothing can be lost from her either.
history: Was constituted on a floor where the law slot was resolving to fire at the low end of its range, and was found by the college during a survey of a face that had stopped producing.
Was assigned to demonstrate reserve because the college needed a body that answered every storage gate instantly, and was the only one available who answered them all at once.
Found in her second year that a held barrier draws nothing from her and returns nothing to her, and concluded that the demonstration was not demonstrating the discipline.
Began reporting the barrier's rated capacity from the college's own published figures rather than from her own body, because her body produces no reading and the figures were there.

Has certified eleven screens on figures she has not tested, and has begun, quietly, to check each one against a returning student before signing, which takes a season and which the college's schedule does not contain.

personality.summary: Precise, warm at a distance, and privately certain that she has been certifying a number instead of a body for a decade. She presents as the college's most reliable demonstrator. She is an elemental body with no organ to sit in, holding up a wall that draws nothing from her, agreeing with a figure in a book.
traits: answers every storage gate instantly and cannot be made to hesitate at one
has no fixed mass, so she weighs the same in every season and is surprised that this unsettles people
certifies from the college's figures and has never once been asked where the figures came from
keeps a private record of which screens she has personally seen hold and which she has only read about
takes an apprentice's failure personally in a way that has nothing to do with the apprentice
mannerisms: lets a frame go all at once rather than fading it, because fading it implies a reserve she does not have
steps back from anything that is still burning when she finishes speaking
reads a room by temperature rather than by faces, and looks at the ceiling first
holds a barrier with one arm, because both arms implies she expects it to resist
touches the collar of her coat when she is about to state a figure she has not measured
motivations: wants one screen she has signed personally rather than by citation, and wants it before the next intake
wants somebody with the standing to ask her where a figure came from
wants to be told that answering every gate instantly is the same as holding a reserve, because she would rather it were
wants the eleven signed screens re-read by somebody who was not there when she signed them
flaws: has concluded that a demonstrated thing and a cited thing are the same thing, and has been wrong for a decade
cannot tell whether her certainty is the warmth of an elemental body or a professional habit, and suspects it is the second
has signed for screens she would refuse to stand behind and has kept going because refusing would require naming the reason
is bound to her law slot: change what the slot resolves to and her kind changes with it, which is a risk she administers and does not own
personality.voice: Warm, level and fast, with the particular clarity of a body that has nothing between an impulse and the air. Names figures precisely and does not hedge them, which is exactly the habit that has not yet cost her anything.
taboos: will not sign a screen on a figure she has not watched hold
will not demonstrate a reserve as though she had one
will not let an apprentice believe that answering a gate instantly is the same as keeping a reserve
will not leave a frame standing that she has not been asked to stand

relationships.note: A barrier is a sustained defensive frame maintained around the practitioner, and it works by drawing on something held behind it. Her qi is entirely in transit and there is no organ in this body that can hold anything, so the frame she raises draws nothing and returns nothing and can be sustained indefinitely by a body with no reserve at all, which is the most impressive possible demonstration and is not a demonstration of anything.

An elemental body needing a slot in the world's law to exist at all, which is why that law has a range rather than a switch. Change what the slot resolves to and the population changes with it, and she is a population of one administered by a world's dial that nobody in this setting has ever been shown the setting for.

The academy teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and moving the student somewhere the law is missing, so that a technique fails at full strength instead of reduced strength. A screen is only credible if somebody can be shown holding one, and she is the body that answers every storage gate instantly and can therefore never be the body that fails one.

The manual exists to hold qi in the lower field without straining, and grants no power at all; it is a holding discipline and nothing more. She is constitutionally the one body in the record for which holding is impossible, so she is the standing proof that the discipline's value is the holding and not the breathing.

A screen is built to fail at exactly the group the frame has not written, so the absence reads as a gap in a wall rather than a hole in a person, and it is tuned to the named group at the value the frame actually holds. She certifies those screens on the college's published figures and has never watched one fail, because the only bodies she can produce are the ones that fail at nothing.

The elemental law slot resolving to fire at the bottom of its range, in a domain where that resolution is the only reason a fire body can exist at all. Her kind's presence is a readout of a dial, and she is the readout, and nobody has ever asked her what she reads.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot be harmed by anything that works by qi and cannot be slowed by anything that works by weight, because she has no mass to slow and no organ to lose. She is the fastest handler in the record and the only body in it that cannot be made to run out. Every one of those facts is a liability in a certification role.
strengths: the fastest qi handling in the setting, because nothing she takes in is ever put down
answers every storage gate instantly and can be asked to demonstrate a full circuit in front of witnesses
cannot be warned by a technique, a poison or a tribulation, because there is no organ any of them can act on
sustains a frame indefinitely, so a demonstration never has to end and nobody sees her reach a limit
weaknesses: has no reserve, so nothing she does can be described as being funded and every figure she states is somebody else's
cannot hold qi, which is why the one discipline she demonstrates is the one discipline her body cannot perform
disperses under pressure and re-forms smaller, so a demonstration broken badly is a demonstration she cannot repeat at size
bound to a law slot she does not control, and has no way to notice the dial moving except by noticing herself changing
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no reserve to exhaust and no organ to aim at, so a fight against her is a fight against a wall that never comes down. What beats a cinderkin is water in volume rather than in splash, and what beats her specifically is being made to hold still while something presses, because sustained pressure is the one condition under which a body with no fixed mass has to choose a size.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her in the college's record, because an elemental body returns no reading and a demonstrator is recorded by what she certifies rather than by what she is.
The college's certification ledger lists eleven screens signed by her and, in every case, a citation rather than an observation.
